pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_factory/l2/FactoryObservabilityTab.tsx:56 The Factory L2 LLM-spend surface shows a 30-day total and a per-feature breakdown with the untagged bucket visible. It shows no ceiling or run-rate projection, rows cannot be opened to see the calls behind them, there is no outlier view, failed-call spend is not shown, and features past the top 12 are reduced to a 'more' caption, so an anomaly in one call class can hide behind a feature total.

techniques.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_factory/l2/FactoryObservabilityTab.tsx:56 The standard asks for total, then class, then axis, then row. This tab gives the total (line 103) and the per-feature axis, but rows have no drill-down (no onPress), there is no budget or projection, no most-expensive-calls list, no failed-spend series and no default-priced or unattributed share. These are the smells the technique names: 'no way to get from a bar to the calls underneath it' and 'failed-call spend folded invisibly into totals'.

src/features/teams/sub_factory/l2/FactoryObservabilityTab.tsx:41 Spend with no feature tag becomes its own visible 'untagged' row (split by model). It is not dropped or folded into a real feature. Caveat: rows are keyed by the use case's display name rather than a stable id, which conflicts with identity-survives-reuse: a renamed feature splits its history.
src/features/teams/sub_factory/l2/useObservabilityFeeds.ts:47 This context writes no ledger. It reads aggregated pinpoints from the managed project's external LLM tracker over a fixed 30-day window.
src/features/teams/sub_factory/l2/FactoryObservabilityTab.tsx:43 Cost arrives already priced by the external tracker. This context has no price table and does no unit-to-currency conversion.

pairs.registryProposal: spend-observability is written for the product's own spend console. The standard should say whether a read-only, per-project summary of a managed project's EXTERNAL tracker (here Langfuse-style pinpoints) owes the full total-to-row reading order and the self-watch instruments, or only a link out to the tracker's own drill-down. As written, every summary card that shows a spend total is a deviation.
